bearings.paper_claim: Six core tests: Spending(sector, year) = sector baseline + b x Growth(sector, year-k) + c PresidentialYear + d MidtermYear + e ExpectedDemHouse + f ExpectedDemSenate, with k = 0 or k = 1, plus two predicted-growth tests; each run for contributions and lobbying; 72 sector-years (4 sectors x 2008-2025); no regressions run yet.
bearings.paper_location: Text lines 5, 26, 42-56 (opening paragraph; Simple calculations and model)
bearings.system_side: sgs_registry.R encodes the same growth variables (growth_previous_year_pct, growth_same_year_pct, predicted_growth_pct), the same four core controls (pres_year, midterm_year, exp_dem_house, exp_dem_senate) and sector fixed effects. The lobbying specification adds cur_dem_house and cur_dem_senate (SGS_L_CONTROLS, line 34), which the note treats as optional rather than core.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The built study is not the note's scope. The primary sector-year window is 2020-2025 with at least 6 distinct years (SGS_WINDOW_RULE, sgs_registry.R lines 17-18; ruling R8 per sgs_config.R line 34), with a fallback of 10 consecutive years inside 2008-2025 only if the primary fails. The LobbyView tests use the 2008-2025 fallback. The claim that same-year growth is outside a real forecast's information set is not in the note and could not be verified, so it is removed.
bearings.verifier_note: Six-test structure, variables and controls reproduced from text lines 42-56 and the registry. Analyst window 2020-2026 is wrong; code says 2020-2025. Unsupported k=0 forecast-set claim removed. Lobbying control set is wider than the note's four.

bearings.paper_claim: Real growth = 100 x (rev_t / rev_t-1 - 1) on IBISWorld constant-price revenue with no further CPI adjustment. Spending in 2025 dollars = nominal x 321.9 / CPI_year. Democratic share = D / (D + R) by chamber, missing when the denominator is zero. Blanks stay missing, never zero.
bearings.system_side: sgs_run.R lines 281-287 build the dollar-base text for dem-share tests from the base_usd and base_real_m columns, so the denominator is carried explicitly per sector-year. Those lines do not show the zero-denominator missing rule, the growth formula or the CPI multiplier; those were not confirmed in this pass.
bearings.transfer_conditions: IBISWorld covers whole industries while Mentat contributions cover a roster of companies, a population mismatch the note does not state. The attribution of this mismatch to ruling 6 is not in the note and was not verified. IBISWorld historical values may include estimates and later revisions (text line 38).
bearings.verifier_note: Formulas and blank-handling rules reproduced from text lines 20, 32, 36-40 and 58. Ruling-6 attribution removed as unsupported by the note. The code check covered only the dem-share base lines.

bearings.paper_claim: IBISWorld U.S. Key Statistics revenue is in constant prices, so growth ratios need no CPI adjustment. Previous-year growth (k = 1) is one of two actual-growth timings. Predicted growth uses the prior-year forecast for year t; 55 sector-year values, 53 passing the main checks.
bearings.system_side: giving_forecast.py lines 1393-1398 comments describe M = B exp(phi dP + d_h)(1 + x/2), with x taken from the IBISWorld real growth path over the lag window c-3 to c-1, and company PACs exempt (x = 0, D-116). These comments confirm the lagged real-growth input but do not show how the 50/50 weight is derived.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The note supplies only the measurement and lag convention. It says nothing about forecasting giving. The analyst's backtest figures (MAE 3.63 vs 3.99; growth beats naive in 45 percent of targets; LobbyView 2014-2023) were not found in the sector_growth_study folder and are removed. The D-113 attribution for the 50/50 weight is unverified.
bearings.verifier_note: Measurement claims reproduced from text lines 7 and 36-38 and the code comment. Backtest figures could not be located and were dropped. The 50/50 weighting was not traced to a ruling.

bearings.paper_claim: Melange holds bank and CU lobbying aggregates for 1999-2023 and cached annual series for 2021-2025 plus partial 2026 (bank, CU, crypto, fintech). Life insurance and auto are not cached. Organizations still need alignment to the research sectors under one expenditure definition.
bearings.system_side: fec/lobbying/sector_spend.py line 49 sets DEFAULT_YEARS to 2021-2026, consistent with the cached 2021-2025 plus partial 2026 window. The analyst's claim that LobbyView finance classification is name-regex based with coverage reliable through 2021 (vintage 2024-10-25) was not checked.
bearings.transfer_conditions: DEFAULT_YEARS covers the LDA sector-spend build, not the 1999-2023 bank and CU aggregates the note cites. Using LDA spend as an outcome per organization is an identity-source use consistent with D-021; no edge or weight use is implied.
bearings.verifier_note: Inventory claims reproduced from text line 16. Only the 2021-2026 default year window was checked on the system side. Classification-method and vintage claims remain unverified.

related.why: LobbyView is a firm-level LDA database. The note does not name LobbyView as its source for the bank and CU aggregates, so this is background for the LDA measure, not confirmed same-data.
Paul's unpublished client report on financial-services political money covers bank and credit-union sections, overlapping the note's sectors. The note does not cite it.

Its title reports low overlap between lobbying and PAC spending, which is consistent with running contributions and lobbying as separate outcomes. The note does not state this reasoning; it is the analyst's inference.
Its title covers strategic and sequential links between donations and lobbying, a lead-lag framing the note does not use.
Its title covers corporate lobbying, PAC spending and market concentration, a related economic-driver design.
Its title and tags cover the cryptocurrency lobby and PAC spending, the sector the note handles only through a proxy.

summary_issues: Window misstated: the summary says the built study runs a 2020-2026 window. sgs_registry.R and sgs_config.R set the primary window to 2020-2025 (R8), with a fallback inside 2008-2025.
Sector count not established: the summary says nine sectors. sgs_registry.R lines 242 and 463 describe seven study sectors plus community_banks. Treat nine as unverified.

Misattributed quote in paul_alignment: the phrase seems to confirm does not appear in the note. The trend-over-significance rule is not stated in the note either. The note contains no regression results to comment on.

Unlocated figures: MAE 3.63 vs 3.99, growth beating naive in 45 percent of targets, 264 tests with 72 estimable, and retrospective 2023 expected-control fill were not found in the sector_growth_study folder by grep. Unverified.

Numbers present in the study's own review file: sgs_review.R lines 33-35 hold L3-LV base 0.352 and yearfe -0.477, with Holm p moving 0.0375 to 0.1125; lines 237-238 hold adjusted R2 0.884717 vs 0.884690. This is the study's own Codex review, not an independent second path, so it stays UNVERIFIED under DE-062.

Partisan-shift result -0.04 (p 0.76, 2021-25) only partly confirmed: coefficients near -0.0428 and -0.0405 appear in build_receipt_08_contributions_by_chamber.json, but the p-value and window were not located.
Design fidelity overstated: the lobbying tests add cur_dem_house and cur_dem_senate (sgs_registry.R line 34), which the note treats as optional, so the built design is not exactly the note's design.

Giving-forecast link: the 50/50 budget term fed by the IBISWorld lagged real-growth path is supported by code comments (giving_forecast.py lines 1393-1398). The no-out-of-sample-support point rests on the backtest figures, which could not be located.
